methodological_rigor.justification: The study evaluates two open-source AI pathology pipelines across multiple independent cohorts with paired NGS ground truth and H&E whole-slide images, including technical reproducibility checks in TCGA and external testing in US and European datasets (Methods; Results). Performance is quantified with AUCs and confidence intervals (including bootstrap resampling noted in the figure caption) and includes predefined subgroup analyses by ancestry and specimen site (Abstract; Results; Figures). Limitations include the retrospective design, ancestry inference confined to a single cohort, and multiple exploratory subgroup/threshold analyses without clear multiplicity control in the main text (Methods; Limitations; Results).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual multicohort validation study (retrospective cohorts) evaluating a diagnostic/prediction approach, aligning best with Oxford LoE 2b (Abstract; Methods). The clinical relevance is direct because EGFR status guides therapy in lung adenocarcinoma and the proposed triage strategy could reduce rapid testing burden while maintaining high sensitivity/specificity (Abstract; Results; Conclusions). The observed ancestry- and tissue-specific performance variability is also clinically important for equitable deployment and risk management (Abstract; Results; Discussion).

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD is appropriate for prediction-model evaluation and the manuscript states adherence to TRIPOD-AI, describes cohorts, ground-truth mutation profiling, and primary performance metric (AUC) with subgroup evaluations (Methods; Abstract). Reporting includes external validation across DFCI and TNM-I and explicit thresholding/triage strategies with resulting sensitivity/specificity and test-reduction estimates (Results; Conclusions). Although the evaluated models are described as open-source, the normalized manuscript does not describe sharing of the study’s derived datasets or full analysis code/workflows, limiting independent replication beyond re-running the original model codebases.

novelty_literature.justification: The manuscript’s novelty is in independently validating open-source EGFR-from-histology models across large, heterogeneous cohorts and explicitly quantifying performance variability by genetic ancestry and specimen site (Abstract; Results). The comparative finding that one approach generalizes better under domain shift and the dual-threshold triage analysis provide practical deployment insights beyond prior single-dataset validations (Results; Discussion). The work is an applied generalizability/fairness extension rather than a brand-new modeling paradigm, but it fills an important translational gap.

writing_presentation.justification: The abstract is clear on cohorts, sample size, primary metric (AUC), and the key subgroup performance finding, and it ties results to a practical triage use case (Abstract). Methods and results are presented in a logical progression (technical reproducibility, primary cohort testing, external validation, subgroup analyses, thresholding/triage) with concrete numbers (Methods; Results). Figure captions are descriptive (ROC/bootstraps; subgroup bar plots), aiding evaluation in the normalized format (Figures).

key_strengths: Large multicohort validation with paired NGS ground truth and external testing across US and European datasets (Methods; Results).
Transparent, quantitative performance reporting (AUCs with CIs) plus ancestry and specimen-site stratification highlighting equity-relevant variability (Abstract; Results).
Pragmatic deployment analysis using dual-threshold triage with explicit sensitivity/specificity and estimated test-reduction impact (Results; Conclusions).
key_concerns: Retrospective evaluation with limited details in the normalized text on calibration, clinical workflow integration, and prospective impact on time-to-treatment or outcomes (Methods; Conclusions).
Performance degradation in Asian ancestry and pleural samples raises deployment risk and warrants deeper bias/shift analysis and mitigation beyond reporting (Results; Discussion).
Data/code availability for the study’s evaluation pipeline is not described, limiting reproducibility and independent auditing.
chief_reviewer.rationale: A strong applied validation study with direct translational relevance, but subgroup performance gaps and retrospective-only evidence make major revisions appropriate at a tier-2 bar, focused on robustness, calibration, and deployment-risk mitigation.
